## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5, titled *Aññacetāpana* ("Exchanging for something else"), is an analytical rule belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that if a nun receives one item through an attendant or steward but subsequently has it exchanged for something else, the item must be relinquished and the offense confessed. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Direct parallels within the Pali tradition include its corresponding rule in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-np5*) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5. Curated resembling parallels are recognized across several early Buddhist monastic codes under the designation *Aññaviññāpana* ("Requesting something else"), with versions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan translations of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions.
